question.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{3}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int 5\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 5\operatorname{cos}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{3})+C\end{aligned}
$$
